clue.text: Banker not entirely smart to accept award

definitions.note: a river has banks, so in crosswords it is a 'banker'

indicators.note: to accept means the shortened word takes the award inside it
not entirely says the word for smart loses its final letter

parts.note: to smart is to hurt or sting
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A city financier, not wholly clever, agrees to take a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' wants to be a financier; it is a river, something with banks. The Humber is an estuary in north-east England, and the MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords call a river a banker because it flows between banks; the Humber is an English estuary.

clue.text: Diatribe from American resonated amidst shouting

indicators.note: amidst means the American and resonated pieces sit in the middle of the shouting word

parts.note: hue is an outcry, as in 'hue and cry'
rang means resonated, as a bell does

explanation.surface: A rant from a US citizen echoed through the yelling crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: HUE is the old word for a public outcry, kept in the phrase 'hue and cry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, forceful and often angry speech, which is what a diatribe is.

clue.text: Sort of tree, hawthorn, Yank mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned says the words are spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: may is another name for hawthorn blossom, and to yank is to pull; said together they make MAY PULL

explanation.surface: An American talks about the hawthorn as a kind of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American person, but it is the verb meaning pull. MAY PULL said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, the one whose leaf appears on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Brief coalition between opponents becomes apparent

indicators.note: between means the shortened coalition word sits between the two opponents

parts.note: in bridge East and South are opponents, so E and S

indicators.note: Brief says the word for coalition loses its last letter

parts.note: a merger is a joining together, a coalition

explanation.surface: A short-lived alliance between rival parties comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and South sit as opponents, which is why 'opponents' gives two compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, so something that emerges becomes visible or apparent.

clue.text: Accurately remembered cycling to France twice each year

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter is moved round to the end of the string

parts.note: taken as written
F is the international vehicle code for France
twice says the F for France appears a second time
PA, per annum, means each year

explanation.surface: A cyclist who rides to France twice a year knows the route by heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' takes the T at the front of the assembled string round to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known off pat has been memorised so thoroughly that it can be recited perfectly.

clue.text: Decade of lifting restrictions after end of war

indicators.note: after means the restrictions come after the end of war
in a down clue, lifting means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of war

parts.note: ties are restrictions or constraints

explanation.surface: A decade in which restrictions were lifted once the war ended.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lifting' reads a word upwards, so 'of' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: The forties is a ten-year span, such as 1940 to 1949, so it names a decade.

clue.text: Every so often plan to ruin cunning tribal leader

indicators.note: Every so often means only every other letter of the phrase is used

parts.note: taking the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters gives P, A, T, R, I
arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: A wily chief keeps scheming to wreck things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every so often' takes alternate letters of 'plan to ruin', starting with the first: PATRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family or tribe, the leader of a clan.

clue.text: Flower retired TV actor is wearing

definitions.note: in crosswords a flower can be a river, something that flows

indicators.note: is wearing means the reversed TV word goes around the actor like clothing
retired means drawn back, so the word for TV is read backwards

parts.note: a TV is a set
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: A former television star is sporting a flower in a buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is something that flows, a river. The Thames flows through London.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river because a river flows; the Thames is England's best-known river.

clue.text: An English peer rejected acquiring piano and fine sort of table

indicators.note: acquiring means the reversed phrase takes the piano letter inside
rejected means the phrase is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a lord is a peer of the realm
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
F is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A lord turned down a piano and an elegant table.
explanation.walkthrough: A + E + LORD reversed is DROLEA; 'acquiring' puts P inside it to make DROPLEA, then F is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-leaf table has hinged flaps that fold down, a common kind of furniture design.

clue.text: Met criminal godfather, admitting hesitation

indicators.note: admitting means the rearranged letters let the hesitation in
criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone met a crooked Mafia boss who paused before speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is past tense, and forgathered is the past tense of an old word for assembling.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgather is to assemble or gather together, so people who forgathered met up.

clue.text: Oddly overlooked artists unable to make ceremony

indicators.note: Oddly overlooked means the odd-numbered letters are skipped, leaving the second, fourth, sixth and so on

parts.note: the letters of these two words, read with the first, third, fifth and every other odd one skipped

explanation.surface: Strangely ignored, some artists cannot put on a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly overlooked' means passing over the first, third, fifth letters of 'artists unable' and keeping the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a set form of ceremony performed in a fixed order, often religious.

clue.text: Advance payment craftsman tentatively pockets

indicators.note: pockets means the phrase holds the answer inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of craftsman into tentatively

explanation.surface: A cautious workman keeps an upfront fee in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put up before a poker hand is dealt, so a payment made in advance.

clue.text: Disinfectants shifting grime surfaces picked up

indicators.note: shifting means the letters of grime move into a new order
picked up means heard, so the word for surfaces is replaced by one that sounds like it

parts.note: sides are surfaces, as the faces of a box

explanation.surface: Cleaning products shift dirt and are lifted off worktops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges GRIME into GERMI; SIDES, heard, gives CIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Germicides are chemicals that kill germs, which is what a disinfectant does.

clue.text: Laura's juices flowing for play

indicators.note: flowing suggests liquid running freely, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Laura's juices run freely, enough to fill a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Laura's' is ignored; its letters and those of 'juices' rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar is the Shakespeare tragedy about the Roman dictator's assassination.

clue.text: Crossing border, international ordinance essentially son contravenes

indicators.note: Crossing means the other letters lie across the border word, on either side of it
essentially means the central letter of ordinance

parts.note: a fringe is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Crossing a frontier, a son breaks an international ordinance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives N, the centre of 'ordinance'; I N and S sit across FRINGE, with FRINGE between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule is to break it, which is what contravening a law or regulation means.

clue.text: Spaniel type, black male one, goes around following Helen, barking

indicators.note: following means the male one piece comes after the Helen piece

parts.note: B is the pencil grading abbreviation for black

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of Helen are scrambled
goes around means the male and one letters turn round, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A black male dog circles Helen, barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, which is why it signals a rearrangement; it is not the dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blenheim is a red-and-white variety of King Charles spaniel, named after Blenheim Palace.

clue.text: Candidly every two weeks releasing name that Human Resources must replace

indicators.note: releasing means the word lets go of the name letter
must replace means the Human Resources letters take the place of the name letter

parts.note: fortnightly means once every two weeks
HR is the usual abbreviation for Human Resources

explanation.surface: An HR department frankly announces fortnightly that it is releasing someone who must be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: In FORTNIGHTLY, 'releasing' drops N and 'must replace' puts HR in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthrightly means in a direct and outspoken way, the same as speaking frankly or candidly.

clue.text: Mark again registered gratitude ultimately to house painter

indicators.note: to house means the other letters hold the painter inside them

parts.note: regd is the standard abbreviation for registered
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of gratitude

explanation.surface: A painter is officially thanked for decorating a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A Royal Academician is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, so a painter in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To regrade is to assess and grade again, as when an exam script is remarked.

clue.text: More than one leguminous plant is doing badly

definitions.note: the definition is a plural description, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A bean plant is struggling to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a pea-family shrub grown for blue dye, so indigos are a number of such plants.

clue.text: Duty of sailor whenever visited by female

indicators.note: visited by means the female letter comes along to join the end

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: A sailor's job whenever a woman comes aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax charged on imported goods, also called a customs duty.

clue.text: Itinerant German lied and feigned illness

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the letters travel into a new order

explanation.surface: A travelling German told lies and pretended to be sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be ill, usually to avoid work or duty.

clue.text: River in Turkey navigable having been repeatedly excavated

indicators.note: excavated means hollowed out, and repeatedly says it happens to both words, leaving only their outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters give TY
the first and last letters give NE

explanation.surface: A Turkish river can be sailed now that it has been dredged again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is a river in north-east England that runs through Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is a river flowing to the North Sea through Newcastle upon Tyne.

clue.text: Article inspiring enthusiasm outwardly in subject

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the article takes the other letters inside

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: outwardly means just the outside letters of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece stirring up keenness, at least on the surface, about a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' is used literally, breathing in, so the article takes the letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk, essay or piece of work.

clue.text: There might be a rise in those taking this drug

definitions.text: There might be a rise in those taking this drug

parts.words: There might be a rise in those taking this drug
parts.note: reads like a statistic about growing numbers of users, but the rise is the physical effect the drug is taken for

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rising numbers of people taking a drug; the 'rise' is really the effect it has on each man who takes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brand-name medicine for erectile dysfunction, prescribed to help produce an erection.

clue.text: Setter perhaps on and on about flipping nonsense

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so a dog, perhaps

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the combined letters are read backwards
about means the leg word goes around the second on word

parts.note: the on side in cricket is the leg side
re means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: A crossword setter goes on and on about utter rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' wants to be the crossword compiler; it is the dog. The two 'on's mean different things: the leg side in cricket, and 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written comic verse, so it is used for worthless writing or nonsense.

clue.text: Not all unbelief is heresy for Archbishop of Canterbury

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every lack of faith counts as heresy, says the Archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition took in 'for', but that word is only the link; the definition is 'Archbishop of Canterbury'. Geoffrey Fisher held the post from 1945 to 1961 and crowned Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Fisher was the Archbishop of Canterbury who presided at the 1953 coronation.

clue.text: Respect Mike joining established mobile phone company

indicators.note: joining means the Mike letter is attached at the end

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike joins a long-standing mobile phone firm and earns respect.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a UK mobile phone network.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration, the same as respect for someone.
